feedback.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(-4)y(-4)+x(2)y(2)+x(4)y(4).
$$

If $p(t)=k-2t$ and $q(t)=5-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $p(t)$ and $q(t)$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =p(-4)q(-4)+p(2)q(2)+p(4)q(4) \\  & =(k+8)(5-8)+(k-4)(5-2)+(k-8)(5-8) \\  & =(-3k-24)+(3k-12)+(-3k+24) \\  & =-3k-12\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =0 \\ -3k-12 & =0 \\ 3k & =-12 \\ k & =-4\end{aligned}
$$
